short: Claudius launched the conquest that made Britannia a Roman province.
full:
In 43 CE the emperor Claudius, needing a military triumph to secure his shaky claim to power, sent Aulus Plautius across the Channel with around 40,000 men in four legions. After defeating British forces at the Medway and Thames, Plautius halted to let Claudius himself arrive and lead the final advance into Camulodunum (Colchester), where eleven British client kings formally submitted. Claudius spent barely sixteen days in Britain before returning to Rome to celebrate a triumph.

The invasion opened four decades of further campaigning, as Roman forces pushed into Wales and northern Britain against sustained resistance. Britannia became a frontier province garrisoned by three legions, generating revenue from tin, lead and slaves while absorbing a disproportionate share of the army's manpower. It was the only substantial permanent territorial addition made under the Julio-Claudian emperors after Augustus.
